subject: Use GMRF library in R-INLA package?

messages.author: cc27dfd4a9d94026
messages.subject: Use GMRF library in R-INLA package?
parts:
The glmmAK package for current version of R is archived and I'd like to play around with GMRF as I work my way through the Rue & Held text, but would rather not have to use the C library directly if possible. Is it possible to interact with the library through the INLA package now instead? Or any other packages currently available?

Thanks,
K

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Use GMRF library in R-INLA package?
parts:
On 17 Apr 2015, at 20:13, KTM <morrison...@gmail.com> wrote:

The glmmAK package for current version of R is archived and I'd like to play around with GMRF as I work my way through the Rue & Held text, but would rather not have to use the C library directly if possible. Is it possible to interact with the library through the INLA package now instead? Or any other packages currently available?

Yes, there is partial access to the GMRFLib methods vie the inla package interface.
Off the top of my head, here's a (partial) list of the relevant functions (see the help texts for more info).
inla.qsolve
inla.qreordering
inla.qreorderings
inla.qinv
inla.qsample

There is no direct support for access to the Cholesky factors, but you can combine your own calls to inla.qreordering and Matrix::chol, Matrix::Cholesky, or spam::chol (and then regular solve) to compute things using the more low-level techniques, you also need that to compute log-determinants.

inla.qinv calculates the elements of the inverse of Q for which Q_{ij} is nonzero, plus some additional elements.  This gives access to marginal variances and covariances between neighbours.

Q needs to be a sparseMatrix object.

Finn L


Thanks,
K

Hi,

you can use some of it, like

inla.qinv
inla.qsolve
inla.qsample

see the ?inla.qinv, and simular for documentation.

compute reorderings are available as

inla.qreordering

and a list of all implemented is

inla.reorderings
